SOURCE EXCERPT:
A graduate student is eligible to sit the qualifying examination when the student has completed the four core courses with no grade below B, has a cumulative average of 3.3 or higher, and has an approved adviser of record on file with the Graduate School. A student who meets the coursework requirement but not the average may petition the department's graduate committee, which may permit the examination once where the shortfall is attributable to a single semester and the student has since returned above 3.3. The examination is offered twice a year, in January and in August, and a student may attempt it twice. A second failure ends the student's candidacy in the doctoral programme, though the student may apply the earned coursework to the terminal master's degree. The examination is set and graded by a committee of four, at least one of whom is from outside the student's department, and the outside member's vote is recorded separately in the file.
